text:
maria: Hey team — customer reported a hosted /v1/stream generate call that suddenly returns a server 5xx in our billing logs but the client says they got the final chunk. They attached a capture. Anyone seen a mis-count like this?

akash: saw something similar last month. usually comes down to short TCP FIN race or client-side keepalive closing early. do we have gateway logs for that request id?

maria: yes attached gateway id gw-7f4a. gateway log shows a write failure: `Broken pipe (EPIPE)` right after `200 OK` was forwarded to the client. our metering pipeline flagged that as a 5xx failure. customer insists they received token stream up to the last chunk before FIN.

janelle: can you paste the exact gateway snippet?

maria: sure — from gw-7f4a: 
```
[2026-03-04T18:22:11Z] req=gw-7f4a upstream=router-2 status=200 bytes_sent=1423
[2026-03-04T18:22:11Z] req=gw-7f4a write_error=EPIPE: Broken pipe while writing chunked body
[2026-03-04T18:22:11Z] req=gw-7f4a classification=5xx_rule_stream_fail
```

akash: interesting — bytes_sent logged before write_error. that suggests we attempted to write, OS returned EPIPE on the subsequent write. some clients async-close after receiving last chunk but before FIN handshake completes. our classifier treats any write_error from gateway as 5xx. that's probably too aggressive.

ryan.billing: From billing side this is bad — customers get charged for tokens but then it's flagged as an error in dashboards, confusing support. we need a way to mark these as successful if client ACKed last data.

janelle: do we have TCP level ACK info? that would be ideal but we don't store tcp acks. maybe we can look at nginx `last_sent` vs `last_acked` if available in kernel probes?

akash: quick repro idea: curl -N against our streaming endpoint then close the socket right after receiving the last chunk. I can script it. also try node-fetch with `res.body.cancel()` which some SDKs call. if gateway sees EPIPE after `200` and bytes_sent>0 we should treat as client disconnect (499) not internal 5xx.

maria: customer used a proprietary mobile SDK which does aggressive connection reuse + early close on backgrounding. likely they called cancel() on the stream. they provided a short recording showing the UI got the last message then app backgrounded.

janelle: proposed change: update gateway classifier => if status==200 && bytes_sent > 0 && write_error==EPIPE then mark as client_disconnect_for_stream (499-like) and emit billing_ok tag. need SRE signoff.

akash: agree. low-risk. we should add a small TTL window: only reclassify if `time_between_last_chunk_and_write_error < 5s` to avoid masking real internal crashes. add metric to track how many reclassifications occur. Also add an optional `x-client-closed` header detected by gateway that some SDKs set — that would help.

ryan.billing: fine with billing_ok tag if logs show bytes_sent > 0. we need to update billing pipeline filter and internal docs so support doesn't escalate billing disputes. also add a note to invoices that streaming may show transient write errors but tokens billed when bytes_sent > 0.

maria: I started a repro PR in a private gist with curl + node examples. steps included: 
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream 
2) after last `data: [DONE]` received, `pkill -f curl` to simulate app background close
3) observe gw logs show EPIPE and classification 5xx currently

Here's snippet I used: 
```
echo -n '{"model":"x-large","input":"say hi"}' > p.json
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @p.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream > /tmp/out &
sleep 1; pkill -f curl
```

janelle: good repro. can you also record tcpdump around the socket to prove last chunk was sent and ACKed before FIN? that'll convince ops.

akash: will run repro against staging gw and attach pcap. quick heads up: in our staging kernel we saw `send() OK` then subsequent `write()` returns -1/EPIPE because client already closed; but TCP stack might have acknowledged previous segments. so pcap should show ACK for data seq before RST/FIN.

maria: next steps: 1) SRE to add classifier change + ttl window 2) add metric + grafana panel 3) billing update to treat bytes_sent>0 as billed_success 4) update support playbook with repro steps and sample curl commands. ryan can you sign off on billing change?

ryan.billing: signed off contingent on metric that shows reclassifications <1pct of streaming traffic for 24h. also need feature flag to roll back quickly.

janelle: I'll open the patch. tagging @ops-bot to create rollout ticket and feature-flag.

ops-bot: Created ticket RF-2173: "gateway: reclassify EPIPE-after-200 as client_disconnect for streaming" and feature-flag `s/stream-epipe-reclassify`. Assigned to janelle. ETA: 48h staging test, 7d canary.

maria: thanks all — I'll update the customer with repro steps + timeline. :thumbsup:
